judgment.notes: N001 applies to A=E in Eucl(n). In S002, a>n>=1 ensures its positive-exponent condition; in S003 every exponent used is positive. H^a(E)=0 therefore gives D<=a in both branches. Compactness is supplied by H002, and the power estimates have positive exponents and positive finite constants. There are no E/M applications to review.

Finite radius-delta/2 ball covers give finite s-cost and hence finite H^s_delta(E). In the n>=1 branch, the coordinate subdivision yields at most C h^(-n) sets of diameter <=sqrt(n)h, so total a-cost is <=C n^(a/2)h^(a-n). For every fixed delta>0 and epsilon>0, choose h sufficiently small to meet both the diameter bound and cost <epsilon. The nonnegative infimum H^a_delta(E) is then zero at every scale, and its supremum H^a(E) is zero; no exchange of limits is needed. N001 gives D<=a for every a>n, excluding infinity and then any finite D>n. For n=0, nonemptiness makes E the ambient singleton, whose zero-diameter cover gives zero measure at every positive exponent. The resulting bounds force D=0. Nonnegativity and F002 complete exactly N002.
